note: Rewritten to the claim that survived the four independent audits.

problems.original_statement: An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act: when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins. It also has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as a schedule of study visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation both handle the misalignment itself, but neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring is applied; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. What does not exist is a procedure that selects either quantity from the treatment and observation processes alone, without touching outcome information, together with a reported measure of how far the estimate would have moved under the alternatives.
problems.correction_note: Two additions. A selection tool for the time grid does exist, using cross-validated variance as a measure of data support, and it uses outcome information, so it is a procedure and not an outcome-blind one. And alternative grace periods are not competing specifications of one estimand: they define different treatment strategies and potentially different estimands, so presenting them as a sensitivity analysis misdescribes what is varying.
problems.statement: An emulated protocol has to fix three times that a randomized trial fixes in one act, when eligibility is assessed, when treatment is assigned, and when follow-up begins, and it has to fix the resolution at which time is measured, because routine data arrive as dated records rather than as scheduled visits. Clone-censor-weight and sequential emulation handle the misalignment; neither chooses the grace period or the interval width, and estimates move with both. A coarse interval lets treatment affect an outcome inside the interval before censoring applies; a fine interval produces high-dimensional nuisance models and unstable weights. Selection tools exist and use outcome information: cross-validated variance has been evaluated as a measure of data support for choosing a discretization. What does not exist is a procedure that selects either quantity from the treatment and observation processes alone with outcome labels masked, and treatment and observation processes without further clinical and causal assumptions cannot identify a uniquely meaningful grace period or guarantee that a grid preserves the relevant ordering. Alternative grace periods are different treatment strategies rather than alternative specifications of one, and are presented as sensitivity analyses of a single estimand.
problems.why_open: The choice is made before any model is fitted, so no model can price it, and selecting by fit to the outcome is the one move that would make it a statistical problem and the move that induces selection. The clinically meaningful interval is a property of the disease and the care process rather than of the data, and no purely data-driven criterion recovers it. Published emulations overwhelmingly report a single specification: a systematic review of 14 comparative studies found the grace period unreported in 36% and ranging from 0 to 180 days when reported, with no study conducting a sensitivity analysis on it.
problems.proposed_direction: Prespecify an outcome-blind grid rule and report post-lock comparisons across plausible grids that hold the estimand fixed, so what varies is the discretization rather than the question. Present alternative grace periods as different treatment strategies with their own estimands, not as a sensitivity analysis of one. Compare landmarking, sequential trials, continuous-time g-computation, counting-process marginal structural models and clone-censor-weighting on the same generated data, scoring the proportion of within-interval ordering conflicts alongside bias and coverage, and report grid invariance as a diagnostic while stating that it reveals sensitivity rather than establishing identification.

prior_work.cite: Hernán MA, Sauer BC, Hernández-Díaz S, Platt R, Shrier I. Specifying a target trial prevents immortal time bias and other self-inflicted injuries in observational analyses. J Clin Epidemiol 2016
prior_work.what_it_does: Names the misalignment of eligibility, assignment and follow-up as the source of immortal time bias and shows that specifying the trial removes it. Treats the grace period as given.

prior_work.cite: Cain LE, Robins JM, Lanoy E, Logan R, Costagliola D, Hernán MA. Using observational data to emulate a randomized trial of dynamic treatment-switching strategies. Int J Epidemiol 2016;45(6):2038-2049
prior_work.what_it_does: Works an emulation with grace periods and dynamic switching, establishing the design without a criterion for the grace period's length.

prior_work.cite: Maringe C, Benitez Majano S, Exarchakou A, et al. Reflection on modern methods: trial emulation in the presence of immortal-time bias. Int J Epidemiol 2020;49(5):1719-1729
prior_work.what_it_does: A worked clone-censor-weight example that makes the artificial censoring and its weights explicit.

prior_work.cite: Ferreira Guerra S, et al. Impact of discretization of the timeline for longitudinal causal inference methods. Stat Med 2020
prior_work.what_it_does: Shows that discretization changes the parameter and loses confounder information, and evaluates cross-validated variance as a data-support criterion for choosing a discretization. A selection tool, and not an outcome-blind one.

prior_work.cite: Optimal CD4 count for initiating HIV treatment: impact of CD4 observation frequency and grace periods, and performance of dynamic marginal structural models. Epidemiology 2014
prior_work.what_it_does: Quantifies how the optimal dynamic regime shifts with observation frequency and grace-period length.

prior_work.cite: Impact of time zero designation on estimated COVID-19 antiviral effectiveness in observational studies. Am J Epidemiol 2026
prior_work.what_it_does: Compares five time-zero designations in one cohort, a worked example of the multiverse this entry asks for.

prior_work.cite: Reporting and variability of constructing medication treatment episodes in pharmacoepidemiology studies: a meta-epidemiological review. Pharmacoepidemiol Drug Saf 2020
prior_work.what_it_does: Finds the grace period unreported in 36% of 14 studies and ranging from 0 to 180 days when reported, with no study conducting a sensitivity analysis on the assumption.

prior_work.cite: Tankpinou Zoumenou H, et al. Time Partitioning in Target Trial Emulation. arXiv 2026
prior_work.what_it_does: Treats time partitioning as an unresolved problem in its own right rather than an implementation detail.
